headline: Energy cannot be created or destroyed—only transformed
universal_truth: Nothing is truly lost; everything becomes something else
fun_facts: The energy in your breakfast was once sunlight captured by plants through photosynthesis
A single bolt of lightning contains enough energy to toast 100,000 slices of bread
The law of conservation of energy was formalized in 1847, changing physics forever
discussion_questions: What 'energy' do you put into the world—and what form does it take in others?
When something ends, what does it transform into?
Where do you notice energy being wasted that could be redirected?

hook.script: Right now, energy is flowing through you—chemical energy from food, electrical energy in your nerves, thermal energy keeping you warm. And here's the mind-bending part: that energy will never disappear. It will only change form. Forever.

cliff.script: The first law of thermodynamics says energy cannot be created or destroyed. But that raises a question: if energy never disappears, where does it go? What happens to the energy in a candle after it burns out?
cliff.prompt: Where does energy 'go' when it seems to disappear?

options.text: It transforms into heat, light, sound, or other forms
options.response: Exactly. Energy disperses into the environment—it never vanishes.

options.text: It gets used up by the process
options.response: It feels that way, but physics shows something more interesting...

fact1.title: Sunlight to Breakfast
fact1.script: The energy in your morning eggs came from chicken feed, which came from plants, which captured sunlight. You are, quite literally, running on stored sunshine. Energy flows through food chains, changing form but never vanishing.

fact2.title: Lightning Power
fact2.script: A single lightning bolt releases about 1 billion joules of energy—enough to toast 100,000 slices of bread. In an instant, electrical potential energy transforms into light, heat, and sound. The same energy, expressed explosively.

fact3.title: Conservation Forever
fact3.script: Julius Mayer and James Joule independently discovered energy conservation in the 1840s. It's one of the most fundamental laws of physics: the total energy of an isolated system remains constant. Nothing truly ends; it only transforms.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Energy conservation applies to more than physics. Your effort, your love, your work—they don't disappear. They become something else in the world. Every act ripples outward, transforming but never truly ending.

outro.script: That's Day 19. Tomorrow, we'll explore your five senses—and discover you have more than you think. Until then, notice energy transforming around you: heat becoming motion, food becoming thought.

growTrack.title: Energy Awareness - Notice the Flow
growTrack.learning_objective: Recognize energy transformations in daily life
growTrack.activity: Today, trace energy through your day: the electricity powering your devices came from somewhere, your food's energy came from somewhere. Pick one object and trace its energy back three steps. Everything is connected.
